A multi-row figure showcasing `movement` applications. Each row is one
application: the left column shows a napari snapshot of a video frame
overlaid with keypoints and short trailing tracks, as the
[`movement` GUI](https://movement.neuroinformatics.dev/latest/user_guide/gui.html)
would show it; the right column shows a metric computed with `movement`.

1. A mouse on an elevated plus maze (EPM), with the occupancy heatmap
of its centroid across the whole session.
2. Two interacting bees, with the relative angle between their head
vectors during interactions.

## Imports and style

```{python}
import sleap_io as sio
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from movement import sample_data
from movement.filtering import (
    filter_by_confidence, rolling_filter, interpolate_over_time
)
from movement.io import load_poses
from movement.kinematics import compute_pairwise_distances
from movement.plots import plot_occupancy
from movement.transforms import scale
from movement.utils.vector import compute_norm, compute_signed_angle_2d

from movement_figures import (
    add_inset_colorbar,
    apply_style,
    data_dir,
    figure_size,
    napari_canvas_screenshot,
    plot_polar_histogram,
    save_figure,
)

apply_style("manuscript")
```

## Application 1: EPM occupancy

We fetch the EPM sample dataset and apply a two-step cleaning pipeline:
a confidence filter followed by a rolling median filter.
We also (lazily) load the corresponding video.

```{python}
epm = sample_data.fetch_dataset(
    "DLC_single-mouse_EPM.predictions.h5", with_video=True
)
epm_video = sio.load_video(epm.video_path)
_, epm_height, epm_width, _ = epm_video.shape

position_conf = filter_by_confidence(
    epm.position, epm.confidence, threshold=0.95
)
epm["position"] = rolling_filter(
    position_conf, window=5, statistic="median", min_periods=2
)
```

We grab a napari canvas screenshot of a single frame, with the tracked
points and a short trailing track "tail". The video is loaded via the
`napari-video` plugin, and the dataset's points and tracks layers are added
via the `movement` napari plugin.

```{python}
EPM_FRAME_SEC = 285  # time (s) of the snapshot; mouse is in an open arm here
EPM_TAIL_SEC = 1     # number of seconds to show in the trailing track tail
epm_frame_index = int(EPM_FRAME_SEC * epm.fps)

epm_napari = napari_canvas_screenshot(
    epm, epm.video_path,
    epm_frame_index,
    tail_length=int(EPM_TAIL_SEC * epm.fps),
    zoom=True,
    display_text=False,
)
```

We also load a grayscale version of the same frame, which will be used
as the background for the occupancy heatmap.

```{python}
epm_frame = epm_video[epm_frame_index].mean(axis=2)  # grayscale
```

## Application 2: relative head angle of two bees

Two female worker bumblebees (*Bombus impatiens*) interacting in a petri dish
with a hexagonal beeswax floor, filmed at 100 fps and tracked with
SLEAP ([Pereira et al., 2022](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-022-01426-1)).
We use the 20 s example clip (frames 21000--23000) from SLEAP's
[datasets page](https://docs.sleap.ai/v1.6.5/reference/datasets/#bees).
The tracks carry no confidence scores, so we skip the confidence
filter. We smooth with a rolling median, then interpolate over short gaps
(e.g. when the bees briefly occlude each other).

```{python}
# TODO: fetch via movement.sample_data once the bees dataset is mirrored.
# Until then, place the files in the (untracked) showcase video inputs.
BEES_DIR = data_dir().parent / "videos" / "showcase" / "inputs"
BEES_VIDEO = BEES_DIR / "bees@21000-23000.mp4"

bees = load_poses.from_sleap_file(
    BEES_DIR / "bees@21000-23000.slp",
    fps=100,  # recording rate. The mp4 clip is encoded at 25 fps for playback
)
bees = bees.assign_coords(individual=["bee-1", "bee-2"]) # Rename individuals
position_smooth = rolling_filter(
    bees.position, window=7, statistic="median", min_periods=2
)
bees["position"] = interpolate_over_time(position_smooth, max_gap=25)
```

We convert positions from pixels to mm, using the dataset's 14 px/mm scale.
The pixel positions are kept for the napari snapshot below.

```{python}
PX_PER_MM = 14  # from SLEAP's datasets page
position_mm = scale(bees.position, factor=1 / PX_PER_MM, space_unit="mm")
```

We take each bee's head vector to point from its thorax to its head,
analogous to the head-to-snout vector in `movement`'s
[head direction example](https://movement.neuroinformatics.dev/latest/examples/compute_head_direction.html).
We prefer it over the forward vector computed from two left-right keypoints,
because one of the bees spends a portion of the clip lying upside down and
the forward vector approach assumes a stable view (either top-down or bottom-up).

The relative head angle is the signed angle from bee 1's head vector to bee 2's:
0° when both face the same way, ±180° when they face opposite ways.

```{python}
thorax = position_mm.sel(keypoint="thor", drop=True)
head = position_mm.sel(keypoint="head", drop=True)
head_vector = head - thorax

relative_angle = compute_signed_angle_2d(
    head_vector.sel(individual="bee-1", drop=True),
    head_vector.sel(individual="bee-2", drop=True),
)
```

We only quantify the relative angle during interactions, defined as
frames in which the two thoraxes are within 1.5 body lengths of each other.
This threshold is generous enough to catch bees touching with
antennae and legs while their thoraxes stay apart.
We take body length as the median head-to-abdomen distance, pooled across
both bees and the whole clip.

```{python}
INTERACTION_BODY_LENGTHS = 1.5

abdomen = position_mm.sel(keypoint="abdo", drop=True)
head_to_abdomen = abdomen - head
body_length = compute_norm(head_to_abdomen).median().item()
print(f"Body length (median head-to-abdomen distance): {body_length:.1f} mm")

thorax_distance = compute_pairwise_distances(
    thorax, dim="individual", pairs={"bee-1": "bee-2"}
)
interacting = thorax_distance < INTERACTION_BODY_LENGTHS * body_length
relative_angle_interacting = relative_angle.where(interacting, drop=True)

n_interacting = int(interacting.sum())
print(
    f"Interacting in {n_interacting} of {interacting.size} frames "
    f"({n_interacting / bees.fps:.2f} s, {interacting.mean().item():.0%})."
)
```

We take the snapshot from within an interaction, with both bees upright and
touching with their antennae and legs, and zoom in on the two bees.

```{python}
BEES_FRAME_SEC = 2.5  # time (s) of the snapshot, within an interaction
BEES_TAIL_SEC = 0.1
bees_frame_index = round(BEES_FRAME_SEC * bees.fps)
assert interacting.isel(time=bees_frame_index), "snapshot not in interaction"

bees_napari = napari_canvas_screenshot(
    bees, BEES_VIDEO,
    bees_frame_index,
    tail_length=round(BEES_TAIL_SEC * bees.fps),
    zoom=True,
    display_text=False,
    point_size=20,  # px; the plugin's default of 10 is hard to see when zoomed out
)
```

## Build the figure

Each application is a row. Row heights follow the aspect ratio of the
napari snapshots, so the images fill the left column without padding.

```{python}
row_aspects = [
    img.shape[0] / img.shape[1] for img in (epm_napari, bees_napari)
]
fig_width, _ = figure_size("double")
fig_height = fig_width / 2 * sum(row_aspects) + 0.6
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(fig_width, fig_height))
grid = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=row_aspects)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Row 1: EPM occupancy                                                #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
ax_epm_napari = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, 0])
ax_epm_napari.imshow(epm_napari)
ax_epm_napari.set_title("Mouse on an elevated plus maze")
ax_epm_napari.axis("off")

ax_heat = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, 1])
ax_heat.imshow(epm_frame, cmap="gray")
BIN_PIX = 30  # bins of 30x30 pixels, covering the whole frame
bins = [
    np.arange(0, epm_width + BIN_PIX, BIN_PIX),
    np.arange(0, epm_height + BIN_PIX, BIN_PIX),
]
plot_occupancy(
    da=epm.position,
    ax=ax_heat,
    bins=bins,
    alpha=0.8,
    cmin=10,  # hide bins with fewer than 10 frames
    norm="log",
)
add_inset_colorbar(ax_heat, "# frames")
ax_heat.set_xlim(0, epm_width)
ax_heat.set_ylim(epm_height, 0)
ax_heat.set_title("Occupancy heatmap")
ax_heat.axis("off")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Row 2: bees relative head angle                                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
ax_bees_napari = fig.add_subplot(grid[1, 0])
ax_bees_napari.imshow(bees_napari)
ax_bees_napari.set_title("Two interacting bumblebees")
ax_bees_napari.axis("off")

ax_polar = fig.add_subplot(grid[1, 1], projection="polar")
plot_polar_histogram(relative_angle_interacting, ax=ax_polar)
ax_polar.set_title("Relative head angle")
```

## Save the figure

```{python}
fig_name = "movement_applications_manuscript"
save_paths = save_figure(fig, fig_name, formats=("pdf", "svg"))
print(f"Saved '{fig_name}' figure to {save_paths[0].parent}.")
```
